verses.1: And this is the law regarding holiness. It is a sacred law.
verses.2: In the place where they slaughter the lamb, they also slaughter the goat. Its blood is then sprinkled on the altar around it.
verses.3: And all of its milk will be brought forth from it, along with the aliyah and the milk that covers the kerev.
verses.4: And we shall remove those two pots, as well as the milk that is on them, and also whatever is on the tables.
verses.5: And the priest who offered the sacrifices burned them as an offering to Jehovah.
verses.6: All that belongs to the priests shall be eaten in a holy place. It is a sacred food, something that should not be eaten at any other time.
verses.7: As a sin, it’s like one of those laws that must be obeyed. The priest who violates these laws will be punished accordingly.
verses.8: And the priest who brings the offering, the one who brings it to the priest, shall be considered as having brought it.
verses.9: And all the offerings that are burned on the altar, and all the sacrifices that are offered in the sanctuary, shall be given to the priest who brings them before God.
verses.10: And every offering that is made in vain and worthless will be considered worthless by all the sons of Aaron.
verses.11: And this is the law regarding the offerings that are to be offered to Jehovah.
verses.12: If they offer us an offering with their hands, and if they offer sacrifices as part of the offering, then they must also offer blood offerings in vessels made of gold. The parts of the sacrifices must also be burned in gold containers.
verses.13: On the bread of life, we offer our sacrifices as an offering to God.
verses.14: And one of all the offerings was to be presented to Jehovah. It was a sacrifice of blood, which the priest would offer to Jehovah. This blood would become a sacrifice for him.
verses.15: And in the offering of sacrifices, the offerings of Solomon’s temple, on the day of his sacrifice, they shall be eaten; nothing shall be left from them until evening.
verses.16: And if it is a sacrifice offered on the day of offering, then it will be eaten on that day. But what remains after that day will also be eaten.
verses.17: And the remnant from the sacrifices on the third day was consumed by fire.
verses.18: And if it is eaten from the offering of sacrifices on the third day, then the one who offers it should not want to eat it. It should not be considered unacceptable. And the person who eats it will be punished.
verses.19: And the carcass that has been contaminated by all kinds of filth shall not be eaten. It must be burned. But the carcass that is clean may be eaten.
verses.20: And the soul that eats the meat of the sacrifices offered to Jehovah, and whose shame are upon it… That soul is marked as unclean by its own people.
verses.21: And the soul will be defiled by all kinds of filth, whether it comes from human beings or from dirty animals. It will also be defiled by any kind of unclean food that is part of the sacrifices offered to Jehovah. Then that soul will be marked as unclean.
verses.22: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.23: I said to the children of Israel, “Do not eat any goat’s milk, nor any sheep’s milk.”
verses.24: And the milk of cows and sheep shall be used for all kinds of purposes; but it shall not be eaten.
verses.25: For any food that is from the sheep offered to Jehovah, and whose soul is marked as belonging to its owner, it is considered holy.
verses.26: And do not eat any blood at all on any of your tables, either for yourself or for the animals.
verses.27: Every soul that eats any kind of blood will be marked by that mark.
verses.28: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.29: I say to the children of Israel, “He who brings his offerings to Jehovah shall bring his sacrifices to Jehovah as well.”
verses.30: Our hands will bring forth the offerings of the LORD. We will offer the milk on the altar. We will bring it to the altar, so that it may be offered before the LORD.
verses.31: And the priest burned the milk that was used for the sacrifice. It became a sign for Aaron and his sons.
verses.32: And the right horn shall be given as a gift to the priest who offers the sacrifices for your offerings.
verses.33: He shall bring the blood of the sacrifices and the milk from Aaron’s sons. It shall be used as a right-hand offering for the sacrifice.
verses.34: For the altar and the altar poles, I took them from among the children of Israel, from the shrines of their gods. I will give them to Aaron, the priest, and to his sons, as an everlasting covenant for all generations of the children of Israel.
verses.35: This is the offering of Aaron and his sons, which Jehovah accepted on the day he presented them as offerings to the priest.
verses.36: For Jehovah commanded to give them, on the day they were slaughtered by the children of Israel, a lifelong covenant for their descendants.
verses.37: This is the law for the offering of sacrifices, for sin and for offerings of thanksgiving, for sacrifices to God, and for offerings of holiness.
verses.38: For Jehovah commanded Moses on Mount Sinai, on the day he commanded the children of Israel to offer their sacrifices to Jehovah in the desert of Sinai.
